title: The Holidays in West Chester: The Christmas Parade, Tree Lightings, Santa Trains and Longwood
seo_title: West Chester Christmas Parade & Holiday Things to Do (2026)
description: West Chester's Hometown Christmas Parade on December 4, township tree lightings, Santa's Express, Christkindlmarkt, White Christmas at Uptown, Longwood and Winterthur, with 2026 dates, times and prices.

sections.heading: How the season runs here
sections.html:
West Chester's holiday season runs on a handful of fixed dates, and the borough's biggest night comes early. The craft fairs start in early November. The weekend before Thanksgiving brings the first Santa trains, the Clover Market and the Kennett light parade, and A Longwood Christmas opens on November 20. Thanksgiving weekend is Small Business Weekend downtown and tree lighting night in Downingtown, Malvern and Upper Uwchlan. Then three days carry most of the season: Friday, December 4, when the Hometown Christmas Parade and the Courthouse tree lighting fill High Street (it's also December's First Friday and the first night of Hanukkah); Saturday, December 5, with Santa at the Square, the Jingle Run, the Coatesville parade and the opening of White Christmas at Uptown; and Saturday, December 12, when Christkindlmarkt takes over Gay Street, Santa poses for free photos on High Street and Downingtown holds its parade.

Everything below is within about half an hour of the Courthouse. Dates are for 2026 and come from the organizers' own pages. Where only last year's details are up, we say so, and this page gets updated as the dates land. For what's on any given weekend, the this weekend page is updated daily.

sections.heading: The Hometown Christmas Parade and tree lighting: Friday, December 4
sections.html:
The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce's Hometown Christmas Parade and Tree Lighting is the biggest night of the year downtown, and the chamber expects about 20,000 people. The chamber's new 28 foot tree is lit at 6:30pm from the steps of the Historic Courthouse, facing High Street, and the parade steps off at 7pm. 6abc's Adam Joseph and B101's Kathy Romano are back as emcees, and this year's parade is inspired by America250, the country's 250th birthday. It goes ahead rain or shine; there is no rain date.

The chamber hasn't posted the 2026 route, road closures or parking yet. December 4 is also December's First Friday, when Downtown West Chester says on-street parking is free after 5pm and many shops stay open late with sales. With a crowd that size, plan to be parked and on High Street well before 6:30. Our parade listing will carry the route and closures once the chamber posts them.

The same night. The Balladeer Carolers sing downtown from 4 to 6pm, Uptown Studio's Holiday Cheer Concert is at 5pm, Hanukkah begins at sundown, and the candlelight tours at Hibernia Mansion open out in Coatesville. Phoenixville lights its own tree at First Friday that evening; our Phoenixville holiday guide has that town's season.

sections.heading: Downtown West Chester through December
sections.html:
Shopping weekends. The Holiday Shop and Stroll on Sunday, November 15, noon to 5pm, is a free stamp card crawl through the shops with a raffle at the end; check in at La Chic Boutique. Small Business Weekend runs Friday, November 27 to Sunday, November 29, and on-street parking downtown is free all weekend (lots and garages aren't included, but they are free on Sundays except the Justice Center Garage). The Holiday Window Decorating Contest runs November 21 to December 12, with a People's Choice vote; winners are announced December 14.

Carolers and Santa sightings. The Balladeer Carolers stroll downtown for free on Fridays from 5:30 to 7:30pm (November 27, December 11 and 18), from 4 to 6pm on parade night, and on Saturdays from noon to 2 (November 28 and December 5, 12 and 19). Santa on the Firetruck rolls through downtown at 3pm on November 28, December 5 and December 19.

Saturday, December 5 is the borough's family day. The Jingle Run and Family Walk, the first one, a 5K and a 2K walk for the Care Center Foundation, starts at 9am, with check in at 7:45 at 10 Church Street; it's $40 and kids 8 and under run free, and online registration closes November 20. That evening Santa at the Square fills Marshall Square Park from 4:30 to 6:30pm (rain date Sunday, December 6). The West Chester Public Library's Holiday Home Tour is listed on the library's site for Saturday, December 5, 10am to 3pm; the ticket details there are still last year's ($45 in advance, $55 on the day), so check before you buy.

Saturday, December 12 is Christkindlmarkt, the Chester County Art Association's seventh outdoor holiday market: more than 100 artists and vendors from 11am to 6pm on Gay Street between Darlington and Matlack and on Church Street between Gay and Chestnut. It's free and rain or shine, the streets in the market close to cars all day, and borough garages and lots charge a $20 special event fee that day. From 2 to 4pm the chamber's Photos with Santa at M&T Bank, 10 North High Street, are free, with a concert by the West Chester Music Academy and free hot chocolate.

Museum and Hanukkah. The Chester County History Center (225 North High Street) decorates its galleries for Season of Lights, December 2 to January 2, Wednesday to Saturday 10am to 4pm, included with admission ($10 adults, $7 seniors, $5 children and students; closed Christmas and New Year's Day). Hanukkah begins at sundown on parade night. Last year Chabad of Chester County held Chanukah at the Courthouse on December 14 at 4:30pm; the 2026 date and time aren't posted yet.

sections.heading: Holiday trains
sections.html:
The West Chester Railroad’s Santa’s Express is the borough's signature holiday ride: 75 minutes in all: 30 minutes to Glen Mills, 15 there and 30 back. Trains run November 21 and 22 at 11am, 1pm and 3pm, then at 11am, 1pm, 3pm and 5pm on November 27 to 29, December 5 and 6, December 12 and 13, and December 19 and 20, according to the railroad's booking calendar. Prices show at checkout. Book now: when we checked on November 5, several December departures were already sold out in coach, and the Table Car (tables of four with a live musician) was gone for all of December 12 and 13. Trains board at Market Street Station, 230 East Market Street (map). The railroad says to arrive 20 minutes early, that its lot holds only one train load of cars, that there are no restrooms on board (portable ones are at both stations) and no strollers, and that tickets are nonrefundable and trains run rain, snow or shine.

The Christmas Tree Train leaves Market Street Station at 8am on Sundays, November 29, December 6 and December 13, for a two hour trip to cut your own tree at Wiggins Christmas Trees. Tickets are $35 for adults and $30 for ages 2 to 12; the tree is extra, $90 for ticket holders in 2026, and Wiggins takes cash or check only. Saws are provided, and Santa is not on this train. On November 5 the November 29 and December 6 trips were already sold out.

At the Brandywine Museum of Art in Chadds Ford, the Brandywine Railroad model trains run from November 14 to January 10, daily 9:30am to 5pm (closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day, closing at 1pm Christmas Eve), with late hours until 8pm on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from December 18 to January 3. Holiday admission is $25 for adults, $23 for seniors 65 and up, $10 for students and ages 4 to 17, and free for 3 and under; the museum's regular online tickets aren't valid during the holiday season. Breakfast with the Trains runs 8:30 to 10am on November 21 and 29 and December 12 and 13 ($35, or $25 for members), and Polar Express pajama nights on Wednesday, December 2 and Friday, December 11, 6:30 to 8pm, pair the book with cocoa and cookies ($25 adults, $15 children for nonmembers). 1 Hoffman's Mill Road (map).

The American Helicopter Museum runs a Model Train Weekend over Thanksgiving weekend, November 27 to 29 (Friday and Saturday 10am to 5pm, Sunday noon to 5pm): $15 adults, $14 for seniors and ages 2 to 12, $13 for veterans, with memberships and library passes not valid that weekend. At SantaFest on Saturday, December 12, 10am to 1pm, Santa arrives by helicopter, with photos, crafts and a cardboard gingerbread contest ($15 adults, $14 ages 2 to 12, members free). 1220 American Boulevard (map).

sections.heading: Tree lightings and parades around West Chester
sections.html:
Kennett Square, Saturday, November 21. The Holiday Light Parade brings about 100 lighted floats, bands and tractors down State Street from 6 to 8pm, and ends with Santa lighting the town tree (Kennett Collaborative).

Saturday, November 28: three at once. Malvern's Christmas on King fills King Street from noon to 4 with food trucks, a beer garden, ice carving, Santa and the Grinch, then moves to Burke Park from 4 to 6 for the tree lighting, Santa photos and free gingerbread decorating for kids under 12; organizers say arrive by 4:50 for the lighting. Light Up Upper Uwchlan, the township's tenth, runs 4 to 6pm at Upland Farm, 301 Pottstown Pike, with parking on Darrell Drive: Santa, carols, cookies and cocoa, face painting, story time in the Farmhouse Museum at 4:15, 4:45 and 5:15, and the tree lit at dusk. Downingtown’s tree lighting is 5:30 to 7pm in Kerr Park, with Santa arriving to light the tree at 6:45.

Exton, Thursday, December 3. West Whiteland’s tree lighting starts at 5:30pm at the Township Building, 101 Commerce Drive, with Santa arriving on a fire truck, hot cocoa and treats, caroling and a School of Rock set (township page).

Saturday, December 5. The Coatesville Christmas Parade steps off at 10am on Lincoln Highway, from Strode Avenue to 11th Avenue, with the theme "A Red, White & Blue Christmas." Organizers close Route 30 from 13th Avenue to Glen Crest Road at 7am, cars left on the route after 7 are towed, and there is no rain date. In Downingtown, Santa visits the Log House in Kerr Park from 10am to 2pm. Tredyffrin's tree lighting is 5 to 7pm at Wilson Farm Park, 500 Lee Road in Wayne, free, with photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus (rain date December 6).

Downingtown, Saturday, December 12. The Good Neighbor Christmas Parade steps off at 3pm at the top of Gable Avenue and runs 1.4 miles along Lancaster Avenue to Green Street, with Santa at the end. There is no rain or snow date (organizers).

As of early November, the townships closest to the borough (East and West Goshen, Westtown, East Bradford and Thornbury) hadn't posted a public tree lighting for 2026. West Goshen and Westtown do hold holiday events for their own residents; check the township newsletters.

sections.heading: Craft fairs and holiday markets
sections.html:
• West Whiteland Holiday Craft Fair, Saturday, November 7, 10am to 2pm, at Church Farm School's Founders Pavilion, 1001 Lincoln Highway, Exton. Free admission and parking; it raises money for the township's Friends of the Parks.
  • Brandywine Critter Sale, Thursday, November 19 to Sunday, November 22, 9:30am to 5pm, at the Brandywine Museum of Art: the museum's handmade critter ornaments, $10 to $35, with specialty pieces up to $250. Cards only, no cash.
  • Craft and Mercantile Holiday Market at Eagleview Town Center, Friday, November 20, from 4:30pm in the Tree Grove across from Restaurant Row: more than 35 makers, live music, local beer and wine, and free gingerbread decorating for kids 12 and under.
  • Clover Market Holiday Market, Saturday and Sunday, November 21 and 22, 10am to 4pm, indoors at the Westtown School Athletic Center (map): about 125 makers and vintage dealers, food trucks, free admission and free parking, and free kids' crafts on Saturday. No pets except service animals.
  • Winterthur Holiday Market, Saturday, November 21, in two sessions (10am to 1pm and 2 to 5pm). It's ticketed ($33 for adults, $12 for ages 3 to 12, members free), and everyone, members included, has to reserve ahead.
  • Chester County Craft Guild Holiday Fine Craft Fair, Saturday, December 5, 10am to 4pm, and Sunday, December 6, 11am to 4pm, at the Ludwigs Corner Fire Hall, 1325 Pottstown Pike, Glenmore: about 30 artists, $5 for adults.
  • Kennett Square Holiday Village Market, December 5, 6, 12 and 13, 11am to 5pm, at The Creamery, 401 Birch Street: more than 40 rotating artisans, food trucks and free admission. Park at the Municipal Garage (100 East Linden Street) or the borough lot at 600 South Broad Street and take the free shuttle; The Creamery's lot is for accessible parking and drop off only.
  • Christkindlmarkt in downtown West Chester, Saturday, December 12, 11am to 6pm (details above).
  • Chester County Library Holiday Craft Show, the 15th, Saturday, December 12, 9:30am to 3pm.

sections.heading: Shows, concerts and holiday films
sections.html:
Uptown! Knauer Performing Arts Center (226 North High Street) carries the most holiday programming in town. Irving Berlin’s White Christmas runs December 5 to 27: Saturday nights at 7:30 and Sunday matinees at 3:30, plus Friday nights at 7:30 on December 11 and 18. Tickets for nonmembers are $51 to $61 for adults and $46 to $56 for students, fees included, and the Sunday, December 6 matinee is a $28 Community Day. The holiday films are cheap nights out: Elf on November 27, The Polar Express on December 7, Die Hard on December 14, It’s a Wonderful Life on December 21 and How the Grinch Stole Christmas on December 28, all at 7pm; tickets are $7, except Elf ($17 for adults and $12 for kids). The concerts: Ball in the House’s a cappella Christmas (December 8), Emerald Strings (December 9), the Cartoon Christmas Trio (December 15) and A Crooner’s Christmas (December 17). Tickets only through Uptown’s own site.

At West Chester University, the 105th Annual Holiday Program (symphony orchestra, combined choirs, the Criterions and the Pops Orchestra) plays the Asplundh Concert Hall twice on Saturday, December 5, at 3pm and 7:30pm. The university hasn't posted the 2026 ticket price; last year's was $15. Brandywine Ballet’s Nutcracker takes the same stage December 18 to 20: Friday at 6pm and Saturday and Sunday at 11am and 4pm (the Friday 10am show is for school and senior groups), $30 to $50 (Brandywine Ballet). Its Nutcracker Tea is Sunday, November 22, 10 to 11:45am at the History Center, $35.

Free and nearly free concerts. The Brandywine Valley Symphony's brass quintet plays a Historic Holiday Concert at the History Center on Sunday, December 6 at 3pm. The Chester County Concert Band's holiday concert is free, Saturday, December 12 at 2:30pm at Fugett Middle School, 500 Ellis Lane. At Immaculata's Alumnae Hall, the Immaculata Symphony plays its Christmas concert with the West Chester Children's Chorus on Sunday, December 6 at 3pm ($10, students and children free), and Chesco Pops plays Holiday Pops on Friday, December 11 at 7pm. The Chester County Choral Society sings Saturday, December 12 at 7:30pm at the Church of the Good Samaritan in Paoli.

Theater nearby. People’s Light in Malvern runs its holiday panto, Cinderella, from November 18 to January 3, with $30 Community Curtain shows on November 25 at 2pm and December 20 at 7pm, and a relaxed performance with ASL and audio description on December 13 at 2pm. The Farmhouse at People's Light, at the same address, holds its Santa Brunch on Sunday, December 13, 10am to 2pm ($45 adults, $20 kids 12 and under, plus service and tax; reservations required). In Lionville, the Barley Sheaf Players stage The Best Christmas Pageant Ever December 4 to 13: 7pm on December 4, 5, 11 and 12, and 2pm on December 6 (a relaxed performance), 12 and 13; $25 adults, $20 students and seniors.

The Kennett Flash (102 Sycamore Alley, Kennett Square) has John Flynn’s annual holiday concert on December 3, Mama’s Black Sheep on December 10 and Charlie Brown Holiday Jazz on December 11 ($25, $10 for kids 12 and under), all at 7pm.

sections.heading: Longwood, Winterthur and the historic houses
sections.html:
A Longwood Christmas in Kennett Square runs November 20 to January 10, 10am to 11pm daily, on timed tickets, and this year's theme is a cosmic Christmas. Adults 16 to 64 are $45 on off peak dates and $52 on peak ones; ages 5 to 15 are $25 and $32; 4 and under free. Peak means every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from opening and every day from December 18 to January 3, so a Monday to Thursday visit before December 18 is the cheaper one. Members need timed reservations too. Parking is free. Details on our Longwood listing. 1001 Longwood Road (map).

Yuletide at Winterthur, just over the Delaware line on Route 52, runs from November 21 to January 3, Tuesday to Sunday 10am to 5pm (closed Mondays, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day). Yuletide admission is $33 for adults, $31 for seniors 62 and up and students, and $12 for ages 3 to 12, and advance reservations are strongly recommended. Holiday Nights keep it open 5 to 8pm on Fridays and Saturdays from November 27 through December 19 (and January 2), included with admission, and A Christmas Carol with the Farm Hill Players plays December 4 and 5 at 6pm and December 6 at 1pm ($25, $10 under 12). 5105 Kennett Pike (map).

Hibernia Mansion Candlelight Tours run three days only: Friday and Saturday, December 4 and 5, 5:30 to 8pm, and Sunday, December 6, 2 to 4pm. Tickets are $10 for adults and $5 for children 6 to 10, under 5 free, and it's cash only at the door. Parking is free. Hibernia County Park, 1 Park Road, Coatesville (map).

Historic Yellow Springs in Chester Springs holds its free Holiday Stroll on Sunday, December 13, 2 to 5pm, with Santa, refreshments and the village decorated (Historic Yellow Springs). The Malvern History Center's holiday open house is Saturday, December 19, 2 to 4pm, at 1 East First Avenue.

For a free light walk, Delaware County's Festival of Lights at Rose Tree Park in Media is a walk through display with free admission and parking and a tree lighting in early December; the county hasn't posted the 2026 date yet.

sections.heading: Christmas trees
sections.html:
The easiest local cut is the Christmas Tree Train out to Wiggins (above). Wiggins Christmas Trees also sells directly, at its farm on Westtown Thornton Road and at a precut lot at 1301 West Chester Pike. Its site lists Black Friday and weekend hours of 9am to 4pm at the farm but no year or prices, so check before you go.

Linvilla Orchards in Media has posted its 2026 season: cut your own from November 21 to December 23 (closed Thanksgiving Day), weekdays 10am to 4pm and weekends 9am to 4pm, no reservations. The farm lists every cut your own tree at $119 plus tax, mostly 5 to 7 foot Douglas fir. Precut trees are sold daily. Santa is there on weekends from Thanksgiving weekend through December 20, 11am to 5pm with a break from 1 to 2:30, and the farm stays open until 8pm on Fridays, November 27, December 4 and December 11, when the Winter Makers Market runs 3 to 8pm (it's also open weekends, 10am to 4pm, through December 20). There's a synthetic ice rink too.

sections.heading: Between the holidays and New Year's Eve
sections.html:
West Bradford's Community Holiday Bonfire is Tuesday, December 29, 4 to 7pm, at Broad Run Park, 1495 Broad Run Road, with the fire company and Scouts; bring your own s'mores supplies.

On New Year's Eve, Kennett Square's Midnight in the Square drops its sparkling mushroom. Entertainment starts at 7pm, the mushroom is raised at about 8:50pm for families with young kids, and the countdown starts at 11:59. Admission is a nonperishable food donation for Kennett Area Community Service. Longwood’s New Year’s Eve has live music from 4 to 10pm, free with a timed garden ticket. In town, Uptown has a comedy night at 8pm on the 31st and dueling pianos the night before.

sections.heading: The season, in order
sections.html:
• November 7: West Whiteland Holiday Craft Fair.
  • November 14: the Brandywine Railroad opens.
  • November 15: Holiday Shop and Stroll downtown.
  • November 18: Cinderella opens at People's Light.
  • November 19 to 22: Critter Sale at the Brandywine.
  • November 20: A Longwood Christmas opens; Eagleview's holiday market.
  • November 21: Kennett Holiday Light Parade; Clover Market (also November 22); Yuletide opens at Winterthur, with its holiday market; first Santa's Express trains (also November 22); Linvilla's tree season opens.
  • November 22: Brandywine Ballet's Nutcracker Tea.
  • November 27 to 29: Small Business Weekend downtown; Model Train Weekend at the Helicopter Museum; Elf at Uptown and the first Holiday Nights at Winterthur (November 27).
  • November 28: tree lightings in Malvern (Christmas on King), Upper Uwchlan and Downingtown; Santa on the Firetruck.
  • November 29: first Christmas Tree Train.
  • December 2: Season of Lights opens at the History Center; Polar Express pajama night at the Brandywine.
  • December 3: West Whiteland tree lighting; John Flynn at the Kennett Flash.
  • December 4: the Hometown Christmas Parade (tree lighting 6:30pm, parade 7pm); First Friday; first night of Hanukkah; Hibernia candlelight tours begin; The Best Christmas Pageant Ever opens.
  • December 5: Jingle Run; Santa at the Square; WCPL Holiday Home Tour; WCU Holiday Program; White Christmas opens at Uptown; Coatesville parade; Craft Guild fair (also December 6); Kennett Holiday Village Market (also December 6, 12 and 13); Tredyffrin tree lighting.
  • December 6: Historic Holiday Concert at the History Center; Immaculata Symphony; Hibernia's last tours.
  • December 11: Holiday Pops; Charlie Brown Holiday Jazz; Polar Express pajama night.
  • December 12: Christkindlmarkt; Photos with Santa at M&T Bank; SantaFest at the Helicopter Museum; Downingtown parade; Concert Band and Choral Society concerts; library craft show.
  • December 13: Yellow Springs Holiday Stroll; Santa Brunch at People's Light; last Christmas Tree Train.
  • December 18 to 20: Brandywine Ballet's Nutcracker.
  • December 19: Malvern History Center open house; last Santa on the Firetruck.
  • December 20: last Santa's Express trains.
  • December 23: Linvilla's last day for cut your own.
  • December 29: West Bradford's holiday bonfire.
  • December 31: Midnight in the Square in Kennett; New Year's Eve at Longwood.
  • January 3 and 10: Yuletide and Cinderella end, then Longwood's Christmas and the Brandywine Railroad.

Most of these dates are also on the LocalSpot West Chester calendar, and the this weekend page shows what's on in the next few days.
